chunks: Sama‘ah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام:
about wearing a sword in salat (prayer) while it has glue and al-kaymukht on it. He said: “There is no problem so long as you do not know that it is from a dead animal.”

key_terms.السَّيْفِ: the sword being carried or worn during salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْكَيْمُخْتُ: a type of treated leather material
key_terms.تَقْلِيدِ: wearing or hanging something on oneself, here a sword
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; it is permissible
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: a dead animal not slaughtered according to Shar‘i requirements

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear a sword in salat (prayer) if it has glue or leather of uncertain origin on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning carrying or wearing a sword in salat (prayer) when it contains glue or leather material of uncertain origin. The ruling is permissibility unless one knows that the material comes from a carcass, showing that certainty of impurity is required before prohibition applies.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.815 - Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about wearing a sword during prayer that has glue or leather (adhesive substances, such as glue made from animal parts) on it.
Imam (as) replied: "There is no problem as long as you do not know that it is from a dead (non-slaughtered) animal”.
